page.overview:
What is Xalafu?

Xalafu (also known as The Dread One) is a fictional entity created by Peter Levi for his short story "The Life and Death of Zebros Santiago".

Xalafu is a Great Old One who manifests as a great spherical bubble, shiftingly translucent and opaque, covered in colours of disturbing hue, with one gigantic eye seemingly dominating the whole.

The entity is worshipped by a secretive cult operating in a small village near the Crist'bal Col'n mountain in Columbia. The disciples wear black robes while carrying either torches or long staves, and the wizard is garbed in gaudy white and gold robes. When conducting a sacrifice, a human is tied to an altar as the cult repeatedly chants "Ng'gai'ghl rai uflu ph-ngl dtuu v'hss Xalafu ght gai'lall" numerous times until the human starts incomprehensibly screaming. After being beaten by the staff-wielding disciples, the wizard will perform a hand-waving ritual, and pour out a vial of white power known as Diabolusaerugo to cover the human's body, followed by repeatedly chanting "Omm ug'luh vai Ufalax cn-cns'lgh mngl whglg ssi XALAFU!", before exclaiming the previous chants backwards and stepping back.

When the ceremony is complete, the sky will turn a sickly red and the moon will become purple, as an orangish light gleams from a rift in the sky, allowing Xalafu to enter this dimension. Creeping down from the sky towards the altar, Xalafu smothers the area and gorges on the human sacrifice. Upon finishing, Xalafu slowly floats back into the rift and disappears.
